about: M7 deliverable 2 (Strategy, 2026-10-27): LIMB DAMAGE THAT CHANGES THE FIGHT. The M4 rules evaluator (data/rules.json, src/fight/rules-eval.ts, opt-in ?rules=m4) tracks per-part HP on the opponent; this file says what each part at low or zero HP DOES to him in the fight, as rows. Opt-in `?feel=limbs` AND `?rules=m4` (the part HP exists only under the evaluator; ?feel=limbs alone does nothing). Design references (public behaviour only, no code read): Exanima's and Mordhau's limb injury consequences (a crippled leg is a limp and a stumble under a heavy blow; a ruined sword arm drops the guard and the weapon). src/fight/feel-limbs.ts reads every number and name here. WHAT IS PRESENTATION (done in this module): the gait (a periodic dip of the bad leg's physics motors, the good leg dipping a little in antiphase), the sag of a hurt arm, the stumble (both legs give for a moment on a heavy blow), the hunched torso, the lolling head, and the dropped weapon (hidden in his hand, a copy that falls, bounces and lies on the ground). WHAT IS SIM (NOT done here, Strategy's ruling 2026-10-27: it changes the outcome of the fight, so duel.ts and Gate 0 are V3 Dev's): `sim` under each part is the proposal for the numbers the sim should consume (walking pace, turn rate, swing speed, guard arc, damage); this module only EMITS the events named in `events` (through the feel registry, src/fight/feel.ts: ctx.emit, kept on globalThis.__feelEvents) and validates the numbers. INPUT: the sim's per-part budget fractions (feel.setLimbState, read by ctx.limbs(): 1 whole .. 0 gone; keys leg_left, leg_right, arm_left, arm_right, head, torso); when the sim has not handed any (not wired yet) the evaluator's own part HP is the input, read only and on any host (window.__v3Rules.partFractions(): his real part HP in a real fight); the stills set a part through debug.setPartHp, which exists on local hosts only. `limbs.parts.<key>`: `startFrac` the part's HP fraction at which its effect begins (level 0), growing to level 1 at 0 HP (the effect row is scaled by level); `sided` the motor and blend keys are the package's role names and take the part's side (thigh -> thighLeft); `motor` the target motor strength at level 1 per role (1 full, 0.01 limp, docs/API.md setMotorStrength); `blend` how much of the ragdoll's pose replaces the clip's on that bone at level 1 (the motors only show where the bones follow the ragdoll); `gait` (leg): the bad leg's motors dip to `dipTo` for `dipFrac` of each `periodS` (smooth), the good leg dips to `goodDipTo` in antiphase; `hipsDropM` and `hipsTiltRad` the pelvis sinks (metres) and rolls toward the bad leg (radians) at level 1, `hipsBaseFrac` of it held all the time and the rest on each dip (the motors alone barely move a standing body: the hips are the limp you see); `stumble` (leg): a heavy blow (`heavyOnly`: a charged or heavy move, the evaluator's own test) while the leg is at level `level` or more drops both legs to `dipTo` (ease-in `inS`, hold `holdS`, up `upS`) and the pelvis sinks `hipsDropM` and rolls `hipsTiltRad` more, at most once per `cooldownS`; `drop` (sword arm): `afterS` seconds after the arm reaches 0 HP the weapon leaves the hand with `velocity` (m/s, in the ragdoll's frame: x right, y up, z forward) and `spin` (rad/s); it falls under `gravity` (m/s2), bounces `bounces` times at `restitution` (a bounce needs a landing speed over `minBounceSpeed` m/s and leaves `bounceFriction` of the sideways speed), lies `restHeightM` above his floor and turns flat over `lieS`; the fall is worked out in the world (an analytic prop, not a Jolt body), so it stays where it fell when he walks on.
